newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugoslavia raises customs duties on car imports.
newsitem.headline: Yugoslavia raises customs duties on car imports.

text.p: Yugoslavia has raised customs duties on imports of new passenger cars to 35 from 25 percent, the Yugoslav government said on Friday.
"The previous favourable conditions for imports of new cars of over 1,500 cc expire on July 31," Yugoslav Trade Minister Borislav Vukovic told a news conference.
Under a new law on customs tariffs, effective as of August 1, cars and certain other products are treated as "specific" because they could be used by the "screw-driver industry," Vukovic said.

He was referring to a frequent practice of importing parts or semi-assembled goods at lower tariffs because they were registered as raw materials or semi-finished products to help raise production in an economy crippled by years of sanctions and mismanagement.
The new customs tariffs are meant as a disincentive for importers of disassembled or semi-assembled items that need only slight additional work, Vukovic said.
Second hand cars, which can only be imported by Yugoslavs who have lived abroad for a certain number of years, will be subject to a 40 percent customs duty.
Additional taxes payable in the country push the prices of imported cars up by as much as 80 percent of their price on foreign markets.
The Yugoslav government early this year set an import quota of 12,000 cars for 1997.
